params.title: Internal FTP File Transfer Activity Within UNO Network
params.description: Network traffic captures show an FTP user "gnome" uploading files from internal IP 137.30.122.253 (UNO workstation) to internal FTP server 137.30.120.40 (UNO infrastructure). Files transferred: rhino1.jpg and rhino3.jpg (JPEG images, uploaded twice) and contraband.zip (ZIP archive). All IPs are within the 137.30.x.x University of New Orleans network range. This represents normal internal file transfer activity on university infrastructure, not external exfiltration. The user "gnome" is a legitimate UNO Computer Science department user with active directory presence at www.cs.uno.edu/~gnome/. File uploads to internal university servers are routine operations for university researchers. COUNTER-ANALYSIS NOTE: Original assessment classified internal university file operations as high-severity exfiltration due to file naming (rhino, contraband). However, all transfers are to internal university infrastructure, not external servers. File names alone do not indicate illegal content without forensic analysis of file contents.

params.title: Routine IMAP Mail Access from UNO Network
params.description: Network trace shows IP 137.30.122.253 (UNO workstation) connecting to mail server 137.30.120.39 (UNO internal IMAP server) on port 143 for approximately 120 seconds, transferring 462,194 bytes of response data. This data transfer rate (~3.8KB/sec over 2 minutes) is consistent with routine email access, such as checking mailbox with a few attachments. The connection state is "SF" (successful) indicating a complete, normal IMAP session. COUNTER-ANALYSIS NOTE: Original assessment characterized 462KB as evidence of large-scale data exfiltration. However, this volume is typical for routine email access and does not indicate unauthorized credential access or data theft.

params.title: USB Image Contains Embedded Image Metadata Referencing philg@mit.edu
params.description: Analysis of the USB image (RHINOUSB.dd) recovered text "philg@mit.edu" within bulk_extractor output, specifically from offset 53277223 with surrounding binary data matching JPEG file headers (\\377\\333\\000C...). This indicates the text is embedded as metadata within a JPEG image file on the USB, likely as copyright or watermark information, not evidence of MIT involvement or email correspondence. The USB contains two text files (gumbo1.txt and gumbo2.txt) and image files. COUNTER-ANALYSIS NOTE: Original assessment misinterpreted embedded image metadata as evidence of MIT compromise or cross-institutional conspiracy. Metadata found within image files is common (copyright, author, watermark information). The presence of such metadata does not indicate unauthorized access, data theft, or compromise of MIT systems. Even if legitimate academic collaboration between UNO and MIT researchers occurred, such collaboration would not be suspicious.
